article_title: Effects of medical communication curriculum on perceptions of Korean medical school students.
citation: Yoo Hyo Hyun, Shin Sein, Lee Jun-Ki. (2018). Effects of medical communication curriculum on perceptions of Korean medical school students. Korean Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.3946/kjme.2018.106
title: Two-part pre-clerkship medical communication curriculum (LBC + CBC) at a Korean medical school
description: A medical communication curriculum developed on the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation model, comprising a lecture-based curriculum (GC plus theory, 9 class hours over 4 weeks, using role play, MBTI workshops, case studies, and self-reflection) and a clinical skills-based curriculum applying theory with standardized patients. GC was added because 76 students (70.1%) had not covered the subject prior to medical school. It was evaluated with three waves of Likert self-assessments and open-ended perception items.
requirements: Simulation center with standardized patients, tutors, and recording capability; instructional variety in the lecture section
constraints: Post-CBC perceived MC competency showed no significant gain over post-LBC, and MC competency decreased post-CBC per the paired comparisons
target_learning_goals: General and medical communication competency and perceptions of medical communication concepts
examples: Surveys were administered pre-LBC (March), post-LBC (June), and post-CBC (October 2014)
key_sources: Yoo Hyo Hyun, Shin Sein, Lee Jun-Ki. (2018). Effects of medical communication curriculum on perceptions of Korean medical school students. Korean Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.3946/kjme.2018.106
